questions.question_text: Which of these numbers is the largest?

options.why: Chose the largest coefficient without comparing the powers of $10$ first.
Its coefficient beats $6.7$, but a bigger coefficient cannot beat a higher power of $10$.
Read $6.09$ as larger than $6.7$ because it has more digits, but $6.09 < 6.7$.

questions.solution_text:
The highest power of $10$ wins, and at $10^{6}$ the coefficients order as $6.7 > 6.09$.
$6.7 \times 10^{6}$ is the largest.

questions.question_text: Which of these numbers is the smallest?

options.why: Chose the smallest coefficient, but the powers of $10$ must be compared first.
Treated $10^{-4}$ as smaller than $10^{-6}$ because $4 < 6$, but the more negative power gives the smaller number.

questions.solution_text:
The most negative power gives the smallest number: $-6 < -4 < -2$.
$9.6 \times 10^{-6}$ is the smallest.

questions.question_text:
The numbers $3.6 \times 10^{4}$, $3.48 \times 10^{4}$ and $3.09 \times 10^{4}$ all share the same power of $10$.
Which of them is the largest?

options.why: Its coefficient has more digits, but $3.48 < 3.6$ — extra decimal places do not make a number larger.
Compared the final digits instead of the place value of the coefficients — $3.09 < 3.6$.

questions.solution_text:
The powers are all $10^{4}$, so the coefficients decide: $3.6 > 3.48 > 3.09$.
$3.6 \times 10^{4}$ is the largest.

questions.question_text: Which list shows $6.1 \times 10^{2},\ 2.8 \times 10^{4},\ 9.7 \times 10^{3}$ in ascending order?

options.why: Ordered by the coefficients ($2.8 < 6.1 < 9.7$) and ignored the powers of $10$.
Ordered the numbers from largest to smallest instead of smallest to largest.
Compared $6.8$ with $0.000\,74$ at face value — converting first gives $0.000\,74 = 7.4 \times 10^{-4}$, which beats $6.8 \times 10^{-4}$.
The two numbers share the power $10^{-4}$ once converted, but the coefficients $7.4$ and $6.8$ differ.

questions.solution_text:
$0.000\,74 = 7.4 \times 10^{-4}$
The powers are equal, so compare the coefficients: $7.4 > 6.8$.
$0.000\,74$ is larger.

options.why: Compared the coefficients $43$ and $5$ directly, but $43 \times 10^{-4}$ normalises to $4.3 \times 10^{-3}$, which is smaller than $5 \times 10^{-3}$.
Normalising gives $4.3 \times 10^{-3}$, which is close to but not equal to $5 \times 10^{-3}$.

questions.solution_text:
$43 \times 10^{-4} = 4.3 \times 10^{-3}$
The powers are equal, so compare the coefficients: $5 > 4.3$.
$5 \times 10^{-3}$ is larger.

questions.question_text: Which list shows $1.5 \times 10^{-2},\ 3.8 \times 10^{-5},\ 6.3 \times 10^{-4}$ in descending order?

options.why: Treated the more negative powers as larger, reversing the true order.
Ordered by the coefficients ($6.3 > 3.8 > 1.5$) and ignored the powers of $10$.

questions.solution_text:
For negative powers, the power closest to zero is largest: $-2 > -4 > -5$.
